This review covers Blue Magic and two upstream PXT source archives.

The Windows sample, SHA-256 a9d522ef015f45256ccdc85409466338ed3bbe17dea30e035ab13cd1f38cd4c0, is MALICIOUS. Its unsigned version resource calls it a Broadcom hardware monitoring service but also names Blue Magic leak v3.5. The decision rests on implemented theft, extortion and remote control, rather than these names. No runtime execution or successful network transfer is claimed.

Native execution traces recovered with Rizin and Capstone:

- 0x14003f9d0 and 0x140050d90 traverse Chromium profiles, query logins, cookies and payment cards, and decrypt their secrets. 0x140060d90 formats stolen results as PAS:/COO:/HIS:/CRD: messages for the sending routine. Browser app-bound encryption handling includes direct COM attempts and a downloaded chromelevator helper.
- 0x1400294f0 obtains Telegram's tdata path, constructs Copy-Item and Compress-Archive commands using the same staged paths, then passes the session ZIP to curl's Catbox upload. A failed response selects an Invoke-RestMethod PUT to Transfer.sh. This is session extraction alongside browser theft, rather than an isolated backup feature.
- 0x14001d820 opens an input file and a temporary output, resolves CryptAcquireContextA/CryptCreateHash/CryptHashData/CryptDeriveKey/CryptEncrypt/CryptDecrypt through GetProcAddress, selects SHA-256 (0x800c) and AES-256 (0x6610), and reads, transforms and writes chunks. 0x14002e350 calls this transformer. The ransom configuration/UI path at 0x140027ca0 supplies the victim-directed payment demand; 0x1400308b0 persists its encoded wallet/amount configuration. The new hostile rule requires an explicit payment instruction in addition to the existing broader recovery-text trait.
- 0x14004ae80 downloads XMRig/GMiner archives, assembles PowerShell extraction and Defender process exclusions, launches renamed miners, and registers logon tasks and Run values. PowerShell's encoded command is assembled at runtime, rather than stored as a recoverable Base64 script. The extraction text in the binary shows executable selection, copying, exclusions and subsequent execution.
- 0x14006baa0 receives socket data (recv at 0x14006c8f5) and dispatches operator commands. The agent supports keylogging, clipboard monitoring, audio/video/screen capture, remote scripts, miners and ransom controls. An inlined byte-XOR loop at 0x14006cf80 uses key 0x46 to recover proxy_start from stack constants; this is obfuscation of dispatch vocabulary. These are implemented handler paths, not capabilities inferred solely from English strings.
- Entry/startup logic at 0x140706300 checks VM hardware, guest processes and sandbox window classes, then copies the client and registers disguised logon persistence. The single WinJail/MFC-class YARA atom remains suspicious, with its existing Corvus catalogue exclusion.
- TLS callbacks 0x1406034a0 and 0x140603480 implement native runtime initialization/cleanup; 0x140619960 releases per-thread resources. Their coexistence with unrelated analysis-tool strings does not establish TLS anti-debugging. The unsupported correlation was removed. TLS layout, tool references, actual VM probes and the other TLS technique rules were retained.

PXT 5.32.15 (f97861e1bbd804a1a1633ade1defdc2a96bad12b280598d40f2797a52143c62a) and PXT 0.2.145 (e1efd67ede748a5d76219eefc96cad0147c45ca8ad5c89d40fa7f93b702983b0) are BENIGN. Forager fetched both exact versions from proxy.golang.org; both recovered ZIP hashes exactly equal the supplied specimens. The .forage.json sidecars and original artifacts are retained under scratch/bluemagic-pxt/upstream0 and upstream5.

Reviewed archive execution paths include CLI token configuration, child-process wrappers, build/update tasks, device debugging and the simulator. The CLI reads its own configured cloud token, builds requested projects and defaults subprocess wrappers to shell=false. Local development servers use local tokens and default to loopback/localhost. TouchDevelop CompiledScript.init/reinit evaluates generated programs; installPlugin evaluates supplied precompiled plugin code and initializes its runtime. PXT's simulator evaluates msg.code to obtain its entry point. The legacy BingMaps loader adds the vendor mapcontrol script when a map is requested. These features agree with the educational editor/compiler purpose. No compromised build or unauthorized credential acquisition was found in these paths. Installation/deployment context was not supplied.

Fetched GitHub code-view, behaviors, React and React DOM assets are minified web application modules. The code-view module constructs displayed Git push/commit instructions; it does not execute them. The shared Git rule now requires an execution call, and explicitly supports Jake command arrays, preserving the actual git pull in PXT's update task. A redundant generic Git-operation umbrella had no consumers and was removed; working-tree command references remain in their canonical metadata rule. Generic completion-word loop headers from React were moved out of HTTP/device-code into control-flow/status, keeping both original regexes and the OAuth polling consumer's evidence set. These are shared dependency corrections, without a PXT exception. Isolated atomscan reports and cleave facts are retained in scratch; low-tier findings can be stripped from ordinary isolated output.

Validation evidence:

- check.py runs six static specimen controls and four source controls. It changes bytes only in temporary copies and never runs target code. Missing session source, encryption API, hidden launcher, stop verb or payment demand must remove only the corresponding new hostile claims.
- testdata/taxonomy/device-rdp-first-review/check.py: 12 existing cases pass, including hostile OAuth forwarding and its benign controls.
- SC_TT 11032063512.exe and add1f5728133a0bd26f16e14d16e6c39.exe, including its AutoIt members: identical findings with baseline and edited traits. Statement of Account.exe was also checked for the removed TLS correlation and did not match it. No existing positive fixture or external consumer for that correlation was found.
- Original and final atomscan reports include archive members and fetched artifacts. H/S counts: Blue Magic 3/18 -> 6/18; each PXT archive 0/0 -> 0/0. WinJail changes H -> S; the false TLS correlation is removed; four distinct hostile behaviors are added. No supported attack detection is lost. Generic loop evidence is retained under its actual subject, and displayed Git instructions no longer claim execution.
- The benign tile-key-sync extension fixture has a `for (... of pending)` header. Its expected score cap changes 13 -> 14 for the retained neutral header-word observation, which is now explicitly required; max_hostile=0 and max_suspicious=0 remain unchanged.
- ML remains hostile for all three: Blue Magic probability 0.98, each PXT archive 1.0. The latter are classifier false positives despite zero hostile/suspicious rules; no score-driven detections or package exceptions were added.

Run the specimen controls with:

    python3 testdata/triage/bluemagic-pxt-review/check.py <sample.exe> <scratch-dir>

Detailed scans, facts, disassembly and Forager sidecars are in scratch/bluemagic-pxt. The initial scan/facts files are scratch/review/{pe,pxt5,pxt0}.{before,facts}.json.
